Comic strip: a cat thinks in a bubble, "Monday again? Wake me on Friday." Editorial: "The four-day work week could improve worker happiness and productivity." How do the genres share ideas differently?
The comic uses humour and pictures; the editorial uses reasoned argument
Both use thought bubbles
The editorial uses a cartoon cat
The comic presents statistics
Comics use humour and images, while editorials argue with reasons.

Legend: "Long ago, the Great Spirit placed the Thousand Islands like scattered flowers in the river." Geography text: "The Thousand Islands were shaped by glaciers that scraped and exposed ancient rock." How do the texts explain the islands?
The legend gives a traditional explanation; the text gives a scientific one
Both describe glaciers
The geography text tells about the Great Spirit
Both are scientific reports
Legends explain through traditional stories, while geography texts use science.
Recipe: "Whisk two eggs, add milk, and pour onto a hot pan." Story: "Dad whisked the eggs, humming his favourite song, as the smell of pancakes filled the house." What is a key difference?
The recipe gives steps; the story creates a scene
Both give numbered steps
The recipe describes Dad humming
The story lists exact amounts
Recipes instruct, while stories describe characters and settings.

Interview: "Q: Why did you become a firefighter? A: I wanted to help people on their worst days." Short story: "Jamal pulled on his helmet, remembering the fire that had once saved his family's lives." How do the texts present a firefighter?
The interview uses a real person's answers; the story invents a character
Both use questions and answers
The story is a real interview
The interview invents a fictional hero
Interviews record real answers, while short stories create fictional characters.
Haiku: "Spring rain on the roof / tapping softly through the night / seeds wake in the dark." Weather report: "Expect 15 mm of rain overnight, clearing by morning." How do the texts treat rain?
The haiku creates a mood; the report gives a forecast
Both measure rainfall
The report counts syllables
The haiku predicts tomorrow's weather
The haiku uses imagery to create mood, while the report gives measurable predictions.
Advertisement: "Zoom Sneakers — run faster than ever!" Consumer review: "The sneakers were comfortable, but the soles wore out after three months." How do the texts differ in purpose?
The ad tries to sell; the review evaluates honestly
Both try to sell the shoes
The review exaggerates the shoes' speed
The ad points out problems
Ads aim to persuade buyers, while reviews judge the product's strengths and weaknesses.
Play script: "NARRATOR: The storm grew louder. (Thunder sound effect.)" Novel: "The storm grew louder, and thunder shook the windows of the old farmhouse." How do the genres show the storm?
The script uses stage directions; the novel describes it in narration
Both use sound-effect cues
The novel has a narrator label
Neither mentions thunder
Scripts rely on cues for performance, while novels describe events in prose.

Speech: "Friends, we must protect our rivers — for our children and theirs!" Science report: "Tests showed nitrate levels in the river were twice the safe limit." How do the texts address river pollution?
The speech appeals to emotion; the report presents data
Both present test results
The report speaks to friends
The speech lists nitrate levels
Speeches often use emotional appeals, while reports present data.
Graphic novel panel: a girl stares at a huge wave, with the caption "Now or never." Poem: "The wave rose high, a wall of grey, / and still she would not turn away." How do the texts show her courage?
The graphic novel uses an image and caption; the poem uses rhyming lines
Both are only pictures
The poem uses speech bubbles
The graphic novel uses rhyme
Graphic novels combine images and short text, while poems use language patterns like rhyme.
Myth: "Thor's hammer strikes the clouds, and thunder rolls across the sky." Science text: "Thunder is the sound of air expanding rapidly when heated by lightning." How do the texts explain thunder?
The myth uses gods; the science text uses physical causes
Both describe air expanding
The science text mentions Thor
Both are traditional stories
Myths explain nature through gods, while science explains physical causes.

Personal essay: "I was nervous on my first day at a new school, but a girl named Priya waved me over." Guidebook: "New students should report to the main office and pick up a timetable." How do the texts differ?
The essay tells a personal experience; the guidebook gives instructions
Both give instructions
The guidebook describes Priya
The essay lists office hours
Personal essays share experiences, while guidebooks tell readers what to do.

Tall tale: "Paul Bunyan dug the Great Lakes so his blue ox, Babe, would have water to drink." Geography text: "The Great Lakes formed as glaciers melted at the end of the last ice age." How do the texts differ?
The tall tale uses exaggeration; the text gives a scientific explanation
Both describe melting glaciers
The text mentions Babe the ox
The tall tale gives exact dates
Tall tales exaggerate for entertainment, while geography texts explain with science.
Poem: "My grandmother's hands, / wrinkled maps of every road she travelled." Obituary: "Rosa Lee, 92, worked as a nurse for 40 years and raised five children." How do the texts present a grandmother?
The poem uses metaphor; the obituary gives life facts
Both use metaphor
The obituary compares hands to maps
The poem lists her age and job
The poem calls her hands maps, while the obituary lists facts about her life.
Instruction manual: "Step 3: Attach the wheels using the four bolts." Adventure story: "With the last bolt tightened, Eli's homemade go-kart was ready for the big hill." How do the texts differ?
The manual tells how to do a task; the story tells what a character experiences
Both are numbered steps
The manual describes Eli's feelings
The story lists the parts needed
Manuals give procedures, while stories focus on characters and events.

Blog post: "Honestly, the new library is the best thing to happen to our town in years!" Council report: "The library opened on March 1 and recorded 4,200 visits in its first month." How do the texts differ in style?
The blog is informal and opinionated; the report is formal and factual
Both are formal and factual
The report gives the writer's opinion
The blog only lists visit numbers
Blogs are often casual and personal, while official reports are formal and factual.
Lullaby: "Hush now, little one, the moon is watching you." Astronomy article: "The Moon is about 384,400 km from Earth and reflects light from the Sun." How do the texts treat the Moon?
The lullaby uses personification to comfort; the article gives scientific facts
Both give the Moon's distance
The article personifies the Moon
The lullaby explains reflected light
The lullaby gives the Moon human qualities, while the article provides measurable facts.
engXLhIl: One illustration of the Last Spike in 1885 shows a crowd of officials in top hats cheering. Another shows exhausted Chinese railway workers resting beside the tracks. What does the second illustration emphasize?
The workers whose labour built the railway
The officials' celebration
The fancy clothing of the crowd
How easy the work was
Showing tired workers draws attention to the people who did the hard labour.
Two illustrations of Little Red Riding Hood show the wolf. In one, he is a cartoon with a goofy grin; in the other, he looms in dark shadows with glowing eyes. How do the two versions differ in mood?
One is playful; the other is frightening
Both are frightening
Both are playful
Neither shows the wolf
A goofy cartoon feels playful, while shadows and glowing eyes create fear.

A painting shows Jacques Cartier proudly planting a cross at Gaspé in 1534, with Iroquoian people in the background. A modern illustration shows the same scene from the viewpoint of Chief Donnacona, looking worried. What does the modern illustration add?
The Indigenous perspective on the event
A celebration of Cartier's ship
A map of France
The weather that day
Showing the scene through Donnacona's eyes adds the Indigenous viewpoint left out of the older painting.
In one illustration of Robin Hood, he is shown laughing with his merry men around a feast. In another, he aims an arrow from a tree with a serious face. What does each illustration focus on?
One shows his friendships; the other his skill and danger
Both show him eating
Both show him in a tree
Neither shows Robin Hood
The feast highlights friendship, while the aimed arrow highlights skill and danger.
One illustration of the Titanic shows the grand ship sailing proudly in sunshine. Another shows lifeboats in dark, icy water. What does the second illustration emphasize?
The tragedy of the sinking
The ship's luxury
A calm summer voyage
The launch celebration
Lifeboats in icy darkness emphasize the disaster rather than the ship's grandeur.
Two illustrations of Alice in Wonderland show the Mad Hatter's tea party. One uses bright pastel colours; the other uses twisted shapes and dark greens. What effect does the second style create?
It makes the scene feel strange and unsettling
It makes the scene feel calm and normal
It shows the party is at noon
It shows the guests are related
Twisted shapes and dark colours make the scene feel eerie.
An old illustration of Joan of Arc shows her glowing with a halo in shining armour. A modern drawing shows her as a frightened teenager holding a heavy sword. What does the modern drawing emphasize?
Her youth and humanity
Her saintly glory
Her royal crown
Her wealth
Showing her as a scared teenager emphasizes that she was a young, real person.
One illustration of Anne of Green Gables shows her laughing as she runs through a field of flowers. Another shows her crying after Gilbert calls her 'Carrots.' What does each illustration focus on?
One shows her joy; the other her hurt pride
Both show her crying
Both show her in class
Neither shows Anne
The field scene shows happiness, while the crying scene shows her hurt feelings.

A 1914 recruitment poster shows smiling soldiers marching off under a bright sky. A painting from 1917 shows soldiers in muddy trenches at Passchendaele. What does the painting show that the poster leaves out?
The harsh reality of war
How exciting war seemed
The bright weather
The soldiers' clean uniforms
The muddy trench scene reveals the suffering that the cheerful poster hides.

Two illustrations of Jack and the Beanstalk show the giant. In one, Jack is drawn tiny at the bottom of the page while the giant fills the top. In the other, they are drawn the same size. What does the first illustration emphasize?
How small and in danger Jack is
That Jack and the giant are friends
That the giant is harmless
That the beanstalk is short
Drawing Jack tiny beneath a huge giant shows his danger and smallness.

One portrait of Sir John A. Macdonald shows him in formal dress beside a map of Canada. A modern editorial cartoon shows his statue being questioned by students. What does the cartoon invite viewers to do?
Rethink how his legacy is viewed today
Celebrate the map of Canada
Admire his clothing
Learn his birthday
The cartoon asks viewers to reconsider his legacy rather than simply honour him.

In one illustration of The Odyssey, Odysseus is tied to the mast while beautiful Sirens sing. In another, the Sirens are shown as bird-like monsters. How do the illustrators present the Sirens differently?
One makes them alluring; the other makes them monstrous
Both show them as birds
Both show them as sailors
Neither shows the Sirens
One version stresses temptation, the other stresses danger.

Two illustrations show the Underground Railroad. One shows Harriet Tubman leading a group through a moonlit forest. The other shows a family arriving safely in St. Catharines, Ontario. What does each illustration focus on?
One shows the dangerous journey; the other the safe arrival
Both show the arrival
Both show the forest
Neither shows people escaping
The forest scene shows risk, while the arrival scene shows freedom.

In one illustration of Hansel and Gretel, the candy house is bright and cheerful. In another, the same house has crooked windows and is surrounded by dead trees. What does the second illustration hint at?
That the house is a trap
That the house is safe
That it is a sunny day
That the children are home
Crooked windows and dead trees warn of danger inside.

A painting of the Fathers of Confederation shows only men in suits around a table. A modern illustration of the same period shows women and Indigenous people outside the room. What point does the modern illustration make?
Many groups were left out of the decision-making
Everyone attended the meeting
The meeting was outdoors
The men were not important
Placing others outside the room highlights who was excluded.
In one illustration of The Wizard of Oz, the Wizard is a giant green floating head. In another, he is a small man behind a curtain. What does the contrast reveal?
His power is an illusion
He is truly a giant
He is a friendly ghost
He is Dorothy's uncle
The small man behind the curtain shows the huge head was a trick.
Two illustrations of the Klondike show Dawson City. One shows busy saloons and celebrations; the other shows empty streets in winter. What does the second illustration emphasize?
The isolation and hardship of winter
The excitement of the gold rush
Summer festivals
Crowded stores
Empty winter streets emphasize loneliness and hardship.
In one illustration of Peter Pan, Captain Hook is drawn as a comic, clumsy villain. In another, he is a tall, menacing figure with a gleaming hook. How do the versions differ?
One makes Hook funny; the other makes him threatening
Both make him funny
Both make him kind
Neither shows Hook
Comic clumsiness makes him humorous, while a menacing pose makes him scary.
One illustration of the moon landing shows astronauts saluting a flag in triumph. Another shows Mission Control workers anxiously watching screens. What does the second illustration emphasize?
The tension and teamwork behind the mission
The flag on the Moon
The astronauts' spacesuits
The Moon's craters
Showing worried workers emphasizes the effort and stress behind the landing.
Two illustrations of Beauty and the Beast show the Beast. In one, he roars with bared teeth; in the other, he gently holds a rose. What does each illustration emphasize?
One shows his fierceness; the other his gentleness
Both show his anger
Both show him sleeping
Neither shows the Beast
The roar emphasizes fierceness, while the rose emphasizes his gentle side.

A historical illustration of the Battle of Vimy Ridge uses wide views of soldiers advancing in neat lines. A modern illustration shows one soldier's tired face up close. What effect does the close-up create?
It makes the experience feel personal
It shows the whole battlefield
It makes the battle look tidy
It shows the map of France
A close-up of one face helps viewers connect with an individual's experience.
In one illustration of King Arthur, he pulls the sword from the stone as a crowd gasps. In another, he sits alone and grey-haired on his throne. What does each illustration focus on?
One shows the start of his rule; the other its later years
Both show him as a boy
Both show the crowd
Neither shows Arthur
The sword scene shows his rise, while the old king shows later life.
engTpSn: Which topic sentence best introduces this paragraph? …Beavers build dams that create ponds. These ponds provide homes for fish, frogs and birds, and they help prevent floods.
Beavers play an important role in their ecosystems.
The paragraph explains how beavers help other living things and the land.
Which topic sentence best introduces this paragraph? …Students who sleep eight to ten hours remember more, focus better and are less likely to get sick.
Getting enough sleep helps students succeed.
Memory is a part of the brain.
Every detail is a benefit of enough sleep for students.

Which topic sentence best introduces this paragraph? …The Group of Seven painted rugged landscapes of northern Ontario. Their bold colours and brushstrokes created a new style that many saw as truly Canadian.
The Group of Seven helped create a distinctly Canadian style of art.
The details explain how the group shaped Canadian art.
Which topic sentence best introduces this paragraph? …Recycling paper saves trees, and recycling aluminum uses far less energy than making new cans. It also keeps waste out of landfills.
All the details are benefits of recycling for the environment.
Which topic sentence best introduces this paragraph? …First, gather your materials. Next, measure and cut the wood. Finally, sand and paint your birdhouse.
Building a birdhouse takes just a few simple steps.
The paragraph lists the steps for building a birdhouse.
Which topic sentence best introduces this paragraph? …Some volcanoes erupt with explosive blasts of ash. Others release slow rivers of lava. Still others have been quiet for thousands of years.
Volcanoes behave in very different ways.
Each sentence describes a different type of volcanic behaviour.
Which topic sentence best introduces this paragraph? …Cellphones can distract drivers, interrupt sleep and cause neck pain from looking down too often.
Overusing cellphones can cause several problems.
The details are all problems caused by phone overuse.

Which topic sentence best introduces this paragraph? …Inuit traditionally built igloos from blocks of packed snow. The snow trapped warm air inside, while a small entrance tunnel kept the cold wind out.
Igloos were cleverly designed to keep people warm.
The details explain how the igloo's design trapped warmth.
Which topic sentence best introduces this paragraph? …Playing an instrument improves memory and coordination. It also teaches patience and gives people a way to express emotions.
Learning a musical instrument has many benefits.
All the details are benefits of playing an instrument.
Which topic sentence best introduces this paragraph? …The 1918 flu spread quickly among soldiers returning from war. Schools and theatres closed, and about 50,000 Canadians died.
The 1918 flu pandemic had a devastating effect on Canada.
The details show how severely the flu affected Canada.

Which topic sentence best introduces this paragraph? …Bees carry pollen from flower to flower, allowing plants to make fruit and seeds. Without them, many crops like apples and blueberries would fail.
Bees are essential to growing many of our foods.
The paragraph explains how bees make many crops possible.
Which topic sentence best introduces this paragraph? …In the morning, Lena feeds the chickens. At noon, she repairs fences. In the evening, she milks the cows before supper.
A farmer's day is full of hard work.
The paragraph describes a full day of farm chores.
Which topic sentence best introduces this paragraph? …The school added a garden, installed water-bottle filling stations and switched to reusable lunch trays.
Our school has taken several steps to become more eco-friendly.
Each detail is an environmental change made by the school.
Which topic sentence best introduces this paragraph? …Dogs can be trained to guide people who are blind, detect illnesses by smell and find people trapped after earthquakes.
Dogs can help people in remarkable ways.
Some people are allergic to dogs.
All the details are ways dogs assist people.
Which topic sentence best introduces this paragraph? …Ancient Romans built roads, aqueducts and arenas. Many of their designs are still used by engineers today.
Roman engineering continues to influence the modern world.
The details show Roman designs still matter today.
Which topic sentence best introduces this paragraph? …Glaciers store about 69% of the world's fresh water. As they melt, sea levels rise and some communities lose their water supply.
Melting glaciers affect people around the world.
The details explain the effects of melting glaciers on people.
Which topic sentence best introduces this paragraph? …Reading builds vocabulary, improves concentration and lets readers experience lives very different from their own.
Every detail is a benefit of reading.
Which topic sentence best introduces this paragraph? …Hockey began on frozen ponds in the 1800s. Over time, rules were written, leagues formed and the Stanley Cup was first awarded in 1893.
Hockey grew from a pond game into an organized sport.
The details trace hockey's development into an organized sport.
Which topic sentence best introduces this paragraph? …Some students learn best by listening, others by seeing diagrams, and others by doing hands-on activities.
The details describe different ways of learning.
Which topic sentence best introduces this paragraph? …Smoke from the wildfires closed schools, cancelled flights and forced thousands of families to leave their homes.
The wildfires disrupted life across the region.
Each detail shows how the wildfires disrupted daily life.

Which topic sentence best introduces this paragraph? …Monarch butterflies fly up to 4,000 km from Canada to Mexico each fall. They rest in the same forests their ancestors used, though no single butterfly makes the round trip.
The monarch butterfly's migration is an amazing journey.
The details describe the monarch's remarkable migration.
Which topic sentence best introduces this paragraph? …Writers can use social media to share their work instantly, connect with readers worldwide and get feedback right away.
Social media gives writers new opportunities.
All the details describe ways social media helps writers.
engCjAv: Choose the best conjunctive adverb. It was raining heavily; ___, the game was cancelled.
The cancellation is a result of the rain, so consequently fits.
Choose the best conjunctive adverb. I studied hard for the test; ___, I still felt nervous.
Feeling nervous despite studying shows contrast, so nevertheless fits.
Choose the best conjunctive adverb. Maya wanted to see a movie; ___, her brother wanted to go bowling.
The two wishes contrast, so however fits.
Choose the best conjunctive adverb. The museum is free on Tuesdays; ___, it offers guided tours at no cost.
The second idea adds to the first, so furthermore fits.
Choose the best conjunctive adverb. You must wear a helmet; ___, you cannot ride the bike.
Otherwise shows what happens if the condition is not met.
Choose the best conjunctive adverb. We didn't take the bus; ___, we walked to school.
Walking replaced taking the bus, so instead fits.
Choose the best conjunctive adverb. The chef chopped the vegetables; ___, her assistant boiled the water.
The two actions happen at the same time, so meanwhile fits.
Choose the best conjunctive adverb. Wolves live in packs; ___, lions live in groups called prides.
Both animals live in groups, so similarly shows the comparison.
Choose the best conjunctive adverb. The power went out; ___, we lit candles.
Lighting candles is a result of the outage, so therefore fits.
Choose the best conjunctive adverb. Jon forgot his lines; ___, the audience cheered for him.
The cheering happened despite the mistake, so nonetheless fits.
Choose the best conjunctive adverb. The bridge was closed for repairs; ___, drivers had to take a long detour.
The detour is caused by the closure, so as a result fits.
Choose the best conjunctive adverb. The book was long; ___, it was exciting from start to finish.
Being long and exciting contrasts, so however fits.
Choose the best conjunctive adverb. Exercise strengthens the heart; ___, it improves mood.
A second benefit is being added, so in addition fits.
Choose the best conjunctive adverb. Finish your homework first; ___, you can play outside.
Then shows the order of events.
Choose the best conjunctive adverb. The summer was hot and dry; ___, many crops failed.
Crop failure resulted from the weather, so consequently fits.
Choose the best conjunctive adverb. Cats are independent; ___, dogs often crave attention.
The two animals are being contrasted, so in contrast fits.
Choose the best conjunctive adverb. The test was difficult; ___, most students passed.
Passing despite the difficulty shows contrast, so still fits.
Choose the best conjunctive adverb. Many birds migrate south in winter; ___, Canada geese fly to warmer areas.
Canada geese are an example of migrating birds.
Choose the best conjunctive adverb. The team lost its star player; ___, it went on to win the tournament.
Winning despite the loss shows contrast, so nevertheless fits.
Choose the best conjunctive adverb. Turn off the lights when you leave; ___, you will waste electricity.
Otherwise shows the consequence of not turning off the lights.
Choose the best conjunctive adverb. The cafeteria was too crowded; ___, we ate lunch in the library.
Eating in the library was the result of the crowding, so so fits.
Choose the best conjunctive adverb. The scientist repeated the experiment ten times; ___, she got the same result each time.
Indeed emphasizes and confirms the consistency of her results.
engEvBt: Claim: Reading for pleasure improves students' vocabulary.
Students who read 20 minutes a day scored much higher on vocabulary tests than students who rarely read.
Many libraries have comfortable chairs.
Some books have pictures.
My cousin likes comics.
A measured study result directly supports the claim about vocabulary.
Claim: Our school needs a longer lunch break.
A survey showed 70% of students do not have time to finish eating in 30 minutes.
Lunch is served at noon.
Sandwiches are popular.
The cafeteria has blue walls.
The survey directly shows students need more time to eat.
Claim: Wearing seatbelts saves lives.
Transport Canada reports that seatbelts reduce the risk of death in a crash by about half.
Cars come in many colours.
Seatbelts can be uncomfortable.
Many people drive to work.
Official data about fewer deaths directly supports the claim.
Claim: Regular exercise improves mental health.
Research shows people who exercise three times a week report fewer symptoms of anxiety and depression.
Gyms are open late.
Running shoes are expensive.
Some people prefer swimming.
Research linking exercise to better mental health supports the claim.
Claim: Plastic pollution harms ocean wildlife.
Scientists have found plastic in the stomachs of more than half of all sea turtle species studied.
Oceans cover most of Earth.
Plastic is used to make toys.
Turtles live a long time.
Evidence of plastic inside turtles shows direct harm to wildlife.
Claim: Learning to code helps students solve problems.
Students in a coding program improved their problem-solving test scores by 15%.
Computers need electricity.
Coding uses keyboards.
Some games are free online.
A measured improvement in problem-solving supports the claim.
Claim: Trees help cool cities.
Streets with many trees can be up to 5 °C cooler than streets without them in summer.
Trees lose leaves in fall.
Some cities have parks.
Maple syrup comes from trees.
A temperature comparison directly supports the cooling claim.
Claim: Breakfast helps students concentrate.
Teachers in a breakfast-program study reported students were more focused in morning classes.
Cereal comes in boxes.
Some people skip breakfast.
Pancakes are delicious.
Reports of improved focus after breakfast support the claim.
Claim: Many Canadians are learning French.
Enrolment in French immersion programs has grown steadily over the past two decades.
French is spoken in France.
Croissants are French.
Canada has two official languages.
Rising enrolment numbers show more people learning French.
Claim: Bike helmets prevent serious injuries.
Studies show helmets reduce the risk of head injury by about 60%.
Helmets come in many colours.
Bikes have pedals.
Cycling is good exercise.
A statistic on reduced head injuries directly supports the claim.
Claim: Too much screen time harms sleep.
Researchers found teens who used screens within an hour of bedtime slept 30 minutes less on average.
Phones have bright screens.
Some teens like video games.
Bedtime is usually at night.
The study links screen use to less sleep.
Claim: Community gardens bring neighbours together.
Gardeners in a city survey said they met an average of six new neighbours in their first season.
Tomatoes need sunlight.
Gardens can have weeds.
Some people live in apartments.
Survey data on meeting neighbours directly supports the claim.
Claim: Music lessons improve math skills.
Students who took music lessons scored higher on fraction tests than those who did not.
Pianos have 88 keys.
Music can be relaxing.
Some songs are about numbers.
Higher test scores linked to music lessons support the claim.
Claim: The Arctic is warming faster than the rest of the world.
Scientists report the Arctic has warmed nearly four times faster than the global average since 1979.
Polar bears live in the Arctic.
The Arctic is cold in winter.
Snow is made of ice crystals.
Data comparing warming rates directly supports the claim.
Claim: Hybrid buses save the city money.
The city spent 30% less on fuel in the first year after switching to hybrid buses.
Buses carry many passengers.
Some buses are yellow.
Drivers wear uniforms.
Lower fuel spending is direct evidence of savings.
Claim: Pets can reduce stress.
A study found petting a dog for ten minutes lowered people's stress hormone levels.
Dogs need daily walks.
Cats sleep a lot.
Pet food is sold in stores.
Measured lower stress hormones support the claim.
Claim: Later school start times improve attendance.
After one district moved its start time to 8:45, absences dropped by 12%.
School buses are yellow.
Some students walk to school.
Classes last about an hour.
A drop in absences after the change supports the claim.
Claim: Wildfires are becoming more common in Canada.
The area burned by wildfires in Canada in 2023 was more than double any previous record.
Forests have many trees.
Firefighters wear helmets.
Campfires are fun.
Record-breaking burned area supports the claim that fires are increasing.
Claim: Libraries are still important today.
Our local library recorded more than 200,000 visits last year, including thousands for free internet access.
Libraries are quiet.
Books can be heavy.
Some people buy e-books.
High visit numbers show libraries are still widely used.
Claim: Walking to school is good for students' health.
Students who walk to school get about 20 more minutes of physical activity each day.
Sidewalks are made of concrete.
Some students live far away.
Backpacks can be heavy.
Extra daily activity directly supports the health claim.
Claim: Bilingual people have certain thinking advantages.
Studies show bilingual people often switch between tasks more quickly than people who speak one language.
Many countries have two languages.
French uses accents.
Dictionaries are helpful.
Research on faster task switching supports the claim.
Claim: Indoor plants improve air quality.
Some studies have found that certain plants can remove small amounts of chemicals from indoor air.
Plants need water.
Cacti have spines.
Flowers come in many colours.
Research on plants removing chemicals supports the claim.
engCtCl: Claim: Schools should ban junk food. Which is a counterclaim?
Students should learn to make healthy choices on their own rather than have them forced.
Junk food contributes to childhood obesity.
Healthy meals improve concentration.
Many parents support healthier menus.
This opposes the ban by arguing for student choice.
Claim: Every student should learn to play an instrument. Which is a counterclaim?
Instruments are expensive, and not every family can afford one.
Music improves memory.
Playing in a band builds teamwork.
Music lessons teach discipline.
Cost is an argument against requiring instruments.
Claim: Homework should be banned in elementary school. Which is a counterclaim?
Homework helps students practise skills and build study habits.
Young children need time to play.
Homework causes stress at home.
Many families are busy in the evening.
This argues for homework, opposing the claim.
Claim: Cities should build more bike lanes. Which is a counterclaim?
Bike lanes take space from cars and can make traffic worse.
Cycling reduces pollution.
Bike lanes make cycling safer.
More people would bike to work.
This raises a drawback that opposes building bike lanes.
Claim: Video games are good for children. Which is a counterclaim?
Too much gaming can replace physical activity and sleep.
Games can improve hand-eye coordination.
Some games teach problem-solving.
Online games help kids make friends.
This points to harms, opposing the claim.
Claim: Students should be allowed to use phones in class. Which is a counterclaim?
Phones can distract students from lessons.
Phones can be used to look up facts.
Students can use calculator apps.
Parents can reach students in emergencies.
Distraction is an argument against allowing phones.
Claim: The school year should be extended. Which is a counterclaim?
Students and teachers need a long summer break to rest and recharge.
Students forget less with shorter breaks.
More class time improves test scores.
Other countries have longer school years.
This defends the long break, opposing the claim.
Claim: Professional athletes are paid too much. Which is a counterclaim?
Athletes have short careers and bring in huge revenue for their teams.
Teachers earn far less than athletes.
Ticket prices keep rising.
Some athletes earn millions per game.
This justifies high salaries, opposing the claim.
Claim: Fireworks should be banned in residential areas. Which is a counterclaim?
Fireworks are a cherished tradition that brings communities together on holidays.
Fireworks frighten pets.
Fireworks can cause fires.
Loud noises disturb sleeping children.
This defends fireworks, opposing the ban.
Claim: Everyone should become vegetarian. Which is a counterclaim?
Some people have health conditions that make a meat-free diet difficult.
Raising livestock produces greenhouse gases.
Vegetarian diets can lower cholesterol.
Plant foods are often cheaper.
This raises a reason the claim cannot apply to everyone.
Claim: Schools should replace textbooks with tablets. Which is a counterclaim?
Tablets can break easily and cost more to repair than books.
Tablets are lighter to carry.
Digital texts can be updated quickly.
Tablets can include videos.
This points to a drawback of tablets, opposing the claim.
Claim: Gym class should be required every year of high school. Which is a counterclaim?
Some students would benefit more from extra time in academic or arts courses.
Exercise improves mental health.
Many teens do not get enough activity.
Gym class teaches teamwork.
This argues against requiring gym every year.

A tap is a light, quiet sound compared with a bang.

A cartographer makes maps; a lexicographer makes dictionaries.

Each pair is a set of opposites.

engCxAn: Unlike her timid cousin, Rosa loved speaking in front of crowds. What does the word in bold mean?
Rosa loves speaking to crowds, so her cousin is the opposite: shy.
The puppy was docile, but the older dog was wild and hard to control. What does the word in bold mean?
The contrast with wild and hard to control shows docile means gentle.
His room was always immaculate, while his brother's was a mess. What does the word in bold mean?
The opposite of a mess is perfectly clean.
The first speaker was animated, but the second was dull and lifeless. What does the word in bold mean?
The contrast with dull and lifeless shows animated means lively.
Although the soup looked bland, it was actually full of spicy flavour. What does the word in bold mean?
The contrast with full of spicy flavour shows bland means lacking flavour.
Instead of being candid, the witness hid the truth. What does the word in bold mean?
Hiding the truth is the opposite of being candid, so candid means honest.
The arid desert contrasted sharply with the wet rainforest. What does the word in bold mean?
The opposite of wet is dry, so arid means very dry.
The road was treacherous in winter but perfectly safe in summer. What does the word in bold mean?
The contrast with perfectly safe shows treacherous means dangerous.
Her answer was concise, unlike his long, rambling speech. What does the word in bold mean?
The opposite of long and rambling is short and clear.
The once affluent family had become poor after the factory closed. What does the word in bold mean?
The contrast with poor shows affluent means wealthy.
Most students were diligent, but a few were lazy and skipped their work. What does the word in bold mean?
The contrast with lazy shows diligent means hardworking.
He tried to conceal the gift, but his sister revealed it right away. What does the word in bold mean?
Revealed is the opposite, so conceal means hide.
The coach was lenient on Mondays but strict on game days. What does the word in bold mean?
The contrast with strict shows lenient means not strict.
Unlike the serene morning, the afternoon brought a violent storm. What does the word in bold mean?
A violent storm is the opposite, so serene means peaceful.
Instead of being obstinate, Liam was willing to change his mind. What does the word in bold mean?
Being willing to change your mind is the opposite of obstinate, so it means stubborn.
The bread was stale, not fresh like the loaf from the bakery. What does the word in bold mean?
The contrast with fresh shows stale means old and dry.
The new rule was temporary, unlike the permanent changes made last year. What does the word in bold mean?
The contrast with permanent shows temporary means short-lived.
The math problem seemed intricate at first, but the answer turned out to be simple. What does the word in bold mean?
The contrast with simple shows intricate means complicated.
While Jana was optimistic about the game, her brother expected them to lose. What does the word in bold mean?
Expecting to lose is the opposite, so optimistic means hopeful.
The feeble kitten grew into a strong, healthy cat. What does the word in bold mean?
The contrast with strong shows feeble means weak.
The crowd was boisterous during the game but silent during the anthem. What does the word in bold mean?
The contrast with silent shows boisterous means loud and energetic.
Unlike the opaque curtains, the glass let sunlight pour in. What does the word in bold mean?
Glass lets light through, so opaque means blocking light.
engXAnte: What is the antecedent of the pronoun in bold? The puppy wagged its tail at the visitors.
Its refers back to the puppy, whose tail is wagging.
What is the antecedent of the pronoun in bold? After Omar finished the race, he drank a bottle of water.
He refers to Omar, who finished the race.
What is the antecedent of the pronoun in bold? The students handed in their essays on Friday.
Their refers to the students who own the essays.
What is the antecedent of the pronoun in bold? Grandma baked bread, and it smelled wonderful.
It refers to the bread that smelled wonderful.
What is the antecedent of the pronoun in bold? Priya said that she would bring snacks to the party.
She refers to Priya, the one who will bring snacks.
What is the antecedent of the pronoun in bold? The geese flew south because they needed warmer weather.
They refers to the geese that flew south.
What is the antecedent of the pronoun in bold? Marcus and I packed our bags for the camping trip.
Our refers to both Marcus and the speaker.
What is the antecedent of the pronoun in bold? The museum opened its new dinosaur exhibit last week.
Its refers to the museum that owns the exhibit.
What is the antecedent of the pronoun in bold? When the phone rang, Leila answered it quickly.
It refers to the phone that Leila answered.
What is the antecedent of the pronoun in bold? Mr. Chen told the class that he was proud of their work.
He refers to Mr. Chen, the singular male speaker.
What is the antecedent of the pronoun in bold? The team cheered when it won the championship.
It refers to the team acting as a single unit.
What is the antecedent of the pronoun in bold? The scissors were dull, so Ava sharpened them.
Them refers to the scissors that Ava sharpened.
What is the antecedent of the pronoun in bold? The farmers harvested their wheat before the storm.
Their refers to the farmers who own the wheat.
What is the antecedent of the pronoun in bold? The cookies were so good that Ben ate all of them.
Them refers to the cookies Ben ate.
What is the antecedent of the pronoun in bold? Jada practised the piano every day, so she improved quickly.
She refers to Jada, who practised.
What is the antecedent of the pronoun in bold? The river overflowed its banks after the heavy rain.
Its refers to the river whose banks flooded.
What is the antecedent of the pronoun in bold? Ella and Noah visited their grandparents in Halifax.
Their refers to both Ella and Noah.
What is the antecedent of the pronoun in bold? The bicycle needed new tires, so Dad bought them at the store.
Them refers to the plural tires that Dad bought.
What is the antecedent of the pronoun in bold? I lost my keys, but then I found them under the couch.
Them refers to the keys that were found.
What is the antecedent of the pronoun in bold? The bird built its nest in the maple tree.
Its refers to the bird that built the nest.
What is the antecedent of the pronoun in bold? When the actors bowed, the audience clapped for them.
Them refers to the actors who bowed.
What is the antecedent of the pronoun in bold? Aiden's mother said she would pick him up at four.
She refers to Aiden's mother, the one who will pick him up.
engXAgre: Complete the sentence. The dog buried ___ bone in the yard.
Dog is a singular animal, so the possessive its fits.
Complete the sentence. My parents celebrated ___ anniversary in June.
Parents is plural, so the plural pronoun their is needed.
Complete the sentence. Maria packed ___ lunch before school.
Maria is one female person, so her agrees.
Complete the sentence. The committee announced ___ decision on Monday.
Committee acts as one unit here, so its agrees.
Complete the sentence. Both of my brothers lost ___ mittens.
Both is plural, so their agrees.
Complete the sentence. Neither of the boys remembered ___ lines in the play.
Neither is singular and refers to boys, so his agrees.
Complete the sentence. The tree lost all of ___ leaves.
Tree is singular and not a person, so its agrees.
Complete the sentence. Mr. Singh and Ms. Lopez graded ___ tests over the weekend.
Two people joined by and need the plural their.
Complete the sentence. One of the girls left ___ jacket on the bus.
One is singular and refers to a girl, so her agrees.
Complete the sentence. The birds flew back to ___ nests.
Birds is plural, so their agrees.
Complete the sentence. Jamal fixed ___ bike himself.
Jamal is one male person, so his agrees.
Complete the sentence. The company raised ___ prices last year.
Company is singular, so its agrees.
Complete the sentence. My sister and I cleaned ___ room together.
The speaker is included, so the first-person plural our agrees.
Complete the sentence. Each of the women brought ___ own chair.
Each is singular and refers to women, so her agrees.
Complete the sentence. The kittens chased ___ tails.
Kittens is plural, so their agrees.
Complete the sentence. Either Sam or Leo will bring ___ guitar.
With either … or and two singular boys, use the singular his.
Complete the sentence. The school changed ___ start time.
School is a singular thing, so its agrees.
Complete the sentence. The players thanked ___ coach after the game.
Players is plural, so their agrees.
Complete the sentence. Grandpa told ___ favourite story again.
Grandpa is one male person, so his agrees.
Complete the sentence. The band played ___ final song at midnight.
Band acts as one unit, so its agrees.
Complete the sentence. Neither Ana nor her sisters finished ___ chores.
With neither … nor, the pronoun agrees with the closer noun, sisters, which is plural.
Complete the sentence. You should always wear ___ seatbelt.
The subject is you, so the matching possessive is your.
engPnVg: Which sentence has a vague pronoun reference?
When Kai met Leo at the park, he was smiling.
Kai was smiling when he met Leo at the park.
When Kai met Leo at the park, Leo was smiling.
Kai met Leo at the park, and Kai was smiling.
He could mean Kai or Leo, so the reference is vague.
Which sentence has a vague pronoun reference?
On the news, they said a storm is coming.
The news reporter said a storm is coming.
The weather forecast said a storm is coming.
Meteorologists on the news said a storm is coming.
They has no clear antecedent; we do not know who said it.
Which sentence has a vague pronoun reference?
I put the vase on the shelf, and it broke.
I put the vase on the shelf, and the vase broke.
The vase broke after I put it on the shelf.
I put the vase on the shelf, and the shelf broke.
It could mean the vase or the shelf.
Which sentence has a vague pronoun reference?
The teacher spoke to the principal, and she was upset.
The teacher was upset when she spoke to the principal.
The teacher spoke to the principal, who was upset.
The principal was upset when the teacher spoke to her.
She could refer to the teacher or the principal.
Which sentence has a vague pronoun reference?
Maya studied all night for the test, which was a bad idea.
Maya's decision to study all night was a bad idea.
Maya studied all night, but staying up was a bad idea.
Studying all night for the test was a bad idea for Maya.
Which could refer to the test or to studying all night.
Which sentence has a vague pronoun reference?
In the textbook, it explains how volcanoes form.
The textbook explains how volcanoes form.
Chapter 4 of the textbook explains how volcanoes form.
The author of the textbook explains how volcanoes form.
It has no antecedent; the textbook itself should be the subject.
Which sentence has a vague pronoun reference?
Sam told his father that his car needed an oil change.
Sam told his father, "My car needs an oil change."
Sam told his father, "Your car needs an oil change."
Sam said that his own car needed an oil change and told his father.
His could refer to Sam or his father, so it is unclear whose car needs the oil change.
Which sentence has a clear pronoun reference?
Nora asked her coach, "Can I play goalie?"
Nora asked her coach if she could play goalie.
Nora told her coach that she should play goalie.
Nora and her coach agreed that she would play goalie.
The quotation makes clear that Nora is asking about herself.
Which sentence has a clear pronoun reference?
After the cat chased the mouse, the cat fell asleep.
After the cat chased the mouse, it fell asleep.
The cat chased the mouse until it was tired.
When the cat caught the mouse, it was scared.
Repeating the noun the cat removes any doubt.
Which sentence has a clear pronoun reference?
The library closed early because the library's furnace broke.
They closed the library early because it broke.
The library closed early because it was broken, they said.
It closed early because it broke.
Each noun is named, so nothing is unclear.
Which sentence has a vague pronoun reference?
Leah dropped the phone into the bucket, but luckily it wasn't damaged.
Leah dropped the phone into the bucket, but luckily the phone wasn't damaged.
The phone wasn't damaged when Leah dropped it into the bucket.
Luckily, Leah's phone wasn't damaged when it fell into the bucket.
It could mean the phone or the bucket.
Which sentence has a clear pronoun reference?
Ravi's brother said, "Ravi, your shoes are muddy."
Ravi's brother said that his shoes were muddy.
Ravi told his brother his shoes were muddy.
Ravi and his brother noticed his shoes were muddy.
The direct quotation makes clear whose shoes are muddy.
Which sentence has a vague pronoun reference?
They say exercise helps you sleep better.
Doctors say exercise helps people sleep better.
Sleep experts say exercise helps people sleep better.
Research shows exercise helps people sleep better.
They does not refer to any specific person or group.
Which sentence has a vague pronoun reference?
The girls told their mothers that they were going to be late.
The girls told their mothers, "We are going to be late."
The girls said they were going to be late, and their mothers understood.
The mothers learned that their daughters were going to be late.
They could mean the girls or the mothers.
Which sentence has a clear pronoun reference?
When the bus reached the station, the bus driver waved.
When the bus reached the station, he waved.
When it reached the station, he waved at it.
When the bus reached the station, they waved.
The bus driver is named, so the reference is clear.
Which sentence has a vague pronoun reference?
Remove the cover from the pot and wash it.
Remove the cover from the pot and wash the cover.
Wash the pot after removing its cover.
Remove the cover and wash the pot.
It could mean the cover or the pot.
Which sentence has a vague pronoun reference?
Jordan forgot his homework at Ethan's house, which made him angry.
Jordan was angry that he forgot his homework at Ethan's house.
Ethan was angry that Jordan forgot his homework at his own house.
Forgetting his homework at Ethan's house made Jordan angry.
Him could refer to Jordan or Ethan.
Which sentence has a clear pronoun reference?
The baby cried until her father picked her up.
The baby's father picked him up when he cried.
The mother told the aunt that she would hold the baby.
When the baby saw the aunt, she smiled.
Her can only refer to the baby, the only female noun in that sentence.
Which sentence has a vague pronoun reference?
Ellie gave Grace a book after she finished reading it.
Ellie gave Grace a book after Ellie finished reading it.
After finishing a book, Ellie gave it to Grace.
Grace received a book from Ellie, who had finished reading it.
She could mean Ellie or Grace.
Which sentence has a vague pronoun reference?
It says on the poster that the dance starts at seven.
The poster says the dance starts at seven.
According to the poster, the dance starts at seven.
The dance, the poster says, starts at seven.
It has no antecedent; the poster should be the subject.
Which sentence has a vague pronoun reference?
The coach told the referee that he had made a mistake.
The coach told the referee, "You made a mistake."
The coach told the referee, "I made a mistake."
The coach admitted to the referee that the coach had made a mistake.
He could refer to the coach or the referee.
Which sentence has a clear pronoun reference?
Mia's grandmother gave Mia a scarf that the grandmother had knitted.
Mia's grandmother gave her a scarf she knitted.
She gave her a scarf that she had knitted.
Mia and her grandmother had a scarf she knitted.
Naming each person removes any doubt about who knitted the scarf.
engPnAn: What could the pronoun in bold refer to? Jess texted Riley after she left the party.
Both Jess and Riley could be the one who left the party.
What could the pronoun in bold refer to? When Arjun met Theo at the arena, he was wearing a new jersey.
Either boy could be wearing the jersey.
What could the pronoun in bold refer to? The nurse thanked the doctor because she had stayed late.
Either person could have stayed late.
What could the pronoun in bold refer to? Zoe told her aunt that she needed a vacation.
The sentence does not show who needs the vacation.
What could the pronoun in bold refer to? The players told the coaches that they were ready.
Both groups are plural, so they could mean either.
What could the pronoun in bold refer to? Put the plate on the table and clean it.
It could mean either the plate or the table.
What could the pronoun in bold refer to? When Liam called his dad, he was at work.
Either Liam or his dad could have been at work.
What could the pronoun in bold refer to? The girls asked their coach whether she would drive.
She is singular, and the girls are plural, so only the coach fits.
What could the pronoun in bold refer to? The cat chased the mouse until it was exhausted.
Either animal could have been exhausted.
What could the pronoun in bold refer to? Amara and Lily met Hana, and she invited them for lunch.
Them refers to Amara and Lily, so she must be Hana.
What could the pronoun in bold refer to? Mrs. Patel told Ms. Wong that her car had a flat tire.
Either woman could own the car with the flat tire.
What could the pronoun in bold refer to? Dan gave Mark his old skateboard after he bought a new one.
Grammatically, either boy could have bought a new skateboard.
What could the pronoun in bold refer to? The students thanked their teacher because they had passed the exam.
They is plural, and only the students are plural.
What could the pronoun in bold refer to? Take the lid off the jar and wash it.
It could refer to the lid or the jar.
What could the pronoun in bold refer to? Elena, Rosa and Mei walked to school while she told a funny story.
Any of the three girls could be the one telling the story.
What could the pronoun in bold refer to? The scientists told the reporters that they had made an important discovery.
Both groups are plural, so they could grammatically mean either.
What could the pronoun in bold refer to? When the dog saw the cat, it ran under the porch.
Either animal could have run under the porch.
What could the pronoun in bold refer to? Ben's brother told him that his room was a mess.
His could refer to either brother's room.
What could the pronoun in bold refer to? The grandparents visited the twins, and they baked cookies together.
the grandparents, the twins, or all of them
They could mean either group or everyone together.
What could the pronoun in bold refer to? The pilot spoke to the passengers before he took off.
He is singular, and passengers is plural, so only the pilot fits.
What could the pronoun in bold refer to? Kira lent Ana her bike because hers was broken.
Hers could grammatically mean either girl's bike.
What could the pronoun in bold refer to? The waiter brought the chef a plate after he finished his shift.
Either man could have finished his shift.
engPnSh: Which sentence keeps pronoun number and person consistent?
If you want to win, you must practise every day.
If you want to win, one must practise every day.
If you want to win, we must practise every day.
If you want to win, they must practise every day.
The sentence stays in the second person with you throughout.
Which sentence keeps pronoun number and person consistent?
The dogs wagged their tails when the children arrived.
The dogs wagged its tails when the children arrived.
The dogs wagged his tails when the children arrived.
The dogs wagged your tails when the children arrived.
Dogs is plural, so their keeps the number consistent.
Which sentence keeps pronoun number and person consistent?
When we went camping, we saw a moose.
When we went camping, you saw a moose.
When we went camping, one saw a moose.
When we went camping, they saw a moose.
The sentence stays in the first-person plural with we.
Which sentence keeps pronoun number and person consistent?
One should always check one's work.
One should always check your work.
One should always check our work.
One should always check the work we do.
The sentence keeps the pronoun one throughout.
Which sentence keeps pronoun number and person consistent?
Hikers should carry water so that they stay hydrated.
Hikers should carry water so that you stay hydrated.
Hikers should carry water so that he stays hydrated.
Hikers should carry water so that we stay hydrated.
Hikers is plural third person, so they matches.
Which sentence keeps pronoun number and person consistent?
I enjoy swimming because it helps me relax.
I enjoy swimming because it helps you relax.
I enjoy swimming because it helps one relax.
I enjoy swimming because it helps them relax.
The sentence stays in the first person with I and me.
Which sentence keeps pronoun number and person consistent?
The company announced that it would hire new workers.
The company announced that they would hire new workers.
The company announced that we would hire new workers.
The company announced that you would hire new workers.
Company is singular, so it keeps the number consistent.
Which sentence keeps pronoun number and person consistent?
Readers who finish early may choose their next book.
Readers who finish early may choose your next book.
Readers who finish early may choose his next book.
Readers who finish early may choose its next book.
Readers is plural, so their agrees.
Which sentence keeps pronoun number and person consistent?
When you bake bread, you need to let the dough rise.
When you bake bread, one needs to let the dough rise.
When you bake bread, they need to let the dough rise.
When you bake bread, we need to let the dough rise.
The sentence stays in the second person with you.
Which sentence keeps pronoun number and person consistent?
The girls brought their own skates to the rink.
The girls brought her own skates to the rink.
The girls brought your own skates to the rink.
The girls brought its own skates to the rink.
Girls is plural, so their agrees.
Which sentence keeps pronoun number and person consistent?
We should recycle because it protects our planet.
We should recycle because it protects your planet.
We should recycle because it protects their planet.
We should recycle because it protects one's planet.
The sentence stays in the first-person plural with we and our.
Which sentence keeps pronoun number and person consistent?
A student who studies hard will improve his or her grades.
A student who studies hard will improve your grades.
A student who studies hard will improve our grades.
A student who studies hard will improve its grades.
A student is singular third person, so his or her agrees.
Which sentence keeps pronoun number and person consistent?
Visitors must show their tickets at the gate.
Visitors must show your tickets at the gate.
Visitors must show his ticket at the gate.
Visitors must show its tickets at the gate.
Visitors is plural third person, so their agrees.
Which sentence keeps pronoun number and person consistent?
If I forget my lunch, I buy a sandwich.
If I forget my lunch, you buy a sandwich.
If I forget my lunch, one buys a sandwich.
If I forget my lunch, we buy a sandwich.
The sentence stays in the first person with I and my.
Which sentence keeps pronoun number and person consistent?
The team celebrated its victory with a pizza party.
The team celebrated our victory with a pizza party.
The team celebrated your victory with a pizza party.
The team celebrated his victory with a pizza party.
Team acts as a single unit here, so its agrees.
Which sentence keeps pronoun number and person consistent?
When people travel, they should respect local customs.
When people travel, you should respect local customs.
When people travel, one should respect local customs.
When people travel, he should respect local customs.
People is plural third person, so they agrees.
Which sentence keeps pronoun number and person consistent?
You can see the mountains if you look west.
You can see the mountains if one looks west.
You can see the mountains if they look west.
You can see the mountains if we look west.
The sentence stays in the second person with you.
Which sentence keeps pronoun number and person consistent?
The birds returned to their nests at dusk.
The birds returned to its nests at dusk.
The birds returned to your nests at dusk.
The birds returned to her nests at dusk.
Birds is plural, so their agrees.
Which sentence keeps pronoun number and person consistent?
My friends and I love the beach because we can build sandcastles.
My friends and I love the beach because you can build sandcastles.
My friends and I love the beach because one can build sandcastles.
My friends and I love the beach because they can build sandcastles.
My friends and I is first-person plural, so we agrees.
Which sentence keeps pronoun number and person consistent?
Each of the boys raised his hand.
Each of the boys raised your hand.
Each of the boys raised our hands.
Each of the boys raised its hand.
Each is singular and refers to boys, so his agrees.
Which sentence keeps pronoun number and person consistent?
Drivers should slow down when they see a school zone.
Drivers should slow down when you see a school zone.
Drivers should slow down when he sees a school zone.
Drivers should slow down when we see a school zone.
Drivers is plural third person, so they agrees.
Which sentence keeps pronoun number and person consistent?
Before you leave, make sure you turn off the lights.
Before you leave, make sure one turns off the lights.
Before you leave, make sure they turn off the lights.
Before you leave, make sure we turn off the lights.
The sentence stays in the second person with you.
engPnRf: Which sentence uses a reflexive pronoun?
Jaya taught herself to knit.
Jaya herself knitted the scarf.
Jaya knitted the scarf for her.
Jaya and I knitted the scarf.
Herself receives the action of taught, so it is reflexive and cannot be removed.
Which sentence uses an intensive pronoun?
The mayor himself cut the ribbon.
The mayor cut himself on the ribbon.
The mayor cut the ribbon for him.
The mayor and he cut the ribbon.
Himself only adds emphasis; removing it leaves a complete sentence, so it is intensive.
Which sentence uses a reflexive pronoun?
The puppy saw itself in the mirror.
The puppy itself broke the mirror.
The puppy saw it in the mirror.
The puppy saw them in the mirror.
Itself is the object of saw and refers back to the puppy, so it is reflexive.
Which sentence uses an intensive pronoun?
We ourselves painted the mural.
We painted ourselves a mural.
We painted the mural for us.
They painted the mural with us.
Ourselves emphasizes we and can be removed without changing the meaning, so it is intensive.
Which sentence uses a reflexive pronoun?
The players congratulated themselves after the win.
The players themselves organized the party.
The players congratulated them after the win.
The coach congratulated the players after the win.
Themselves is the object of congratulated and refers to the players, so it is reflexive.
Which sentence uses an intensive pronoun?
You yourself said the test would be easy.
You told yourself the test would be easy.
You said the test would be easy for you.
You said it would be easy.
Yourself only emphasizes you, so it is intensive.
Which sentence uses a reflexive pronoun?
I made myself a grilled cheese sandwich.
I myself made the grilled cheese sandwich.
I made a sandwich for me.
My brother made me a sandwich.
Myself is the indirect object and refers back to I, so it is reflexive.
Which sentence uses an intensive pronoun?
The author herself signed my copy of the book.
The author introduced herself to the crowd.
The author signed the book for her.
The author signed my book.
Herself emphasizes the author and can be removed, so it is intensive.
Which sentence uses a reflexive pronoun?
Liam reminded himself to bring his skates.
Liam himself brought the skates.
Liam reminded him to bring skates.
Liam brought his skates.
Himself is the object of reminded and refers to Liam, so it is reflexive.
Which sentence uses an intensive pronoun?

This scarf was knitted for me.
This scarf was knitted by Grandma.
This scarf has been knitted for me.
Grandma is the subject who performs the knitting, so the sentence is active.
engXActW: Which sentence is the active-voice version? The song was sung by the choir.
The choir sang the song.
The song sang the choir.
The choir was sung by the song.
Sang the song, the choir did.
In active voice the doer, the choir, becomes the subject.
Which sentence is the active-voice version? The fence was painted by Leo and Jaya.
Leo and Jaya painted the fence.
The fence painted Leo and Jaya.
Leo and Jaya were painted by the fence.
Painted the fence Leo and Jaya.
Leo and Jaya perform the action, so they become the subject.
Which sentence is the active-voice version? The trophy is held by the captain.
The captain holds the trophy.
The trophy holds the captain.
The captain is held by the trophy.
Holds the trophy, the captain.
The captain does the holding, so the captain becomes the subject in present tense.
Which sentence is the active-voice version? The dishes will be washed by Dad.
Dad will wash the dishes.
The dishes will wash Dad.
Dad will be washed by the dishes.
Will wash the dishes Dad.
The future tense is kept, and Dad, the doer, becomes the subject.
Which sentence is the active-voice version? The streets were cleared by snowplows.
Snowplows cleared the streets.
The streets cleared snowplows.
Snowplows were cleared by the streets.
Cleared the streets, snowplows did.
Snowplows perform the clearing, so they move to the subject position.
Which sentence is the active-voice version? The rules have been explained by the coach.
The coach has explained the rules.
The rules have explained the coach.
The coach has been explained by the rules.
Explained the rules, the coach has.
The coach becomes the subject, and the present perfect tense is kept.
Which sentence is the active-voice version? The bread is being sliced by the baker.
The baker is slicing the bread.
The bread is slicing the baker.
The baker is being sliced by the bread.
Slicing the bread is the baker.
The baker is the doer, and the progressive tense becomes is slicing.
Which sentence is the active-voice version? The new park was designed by an architect.
An architect designed the new park.
The new park designed an architect.
An architect was designed by the new park.
Designed the new park an architect.
The architect performs the action, so the architect becomes the subject.
Which sentence is the active-voice version? The book was recommended to us by the librarian.
The librarian recommended the book to us.
We recommended the book to the librarian.
The book recommended the librarian to us.
The librarian was recommended the book by us.
The librarian is the doer, so the librarian becomes the subject.
Which sentence is the active-voice version? The ice was cracked by the heavy truck.
The heavy truck cracked the ice.
The ice cracked the heavy truck.
The heavy truck was cracked by the ice.
Cracked the ice, the heavy truck.
The truck performs the cracking, so it becomes the subject.
Which sentence is the active-voice version? The essays are graded by Ms. Okafor.
Ms. Okafor grades the essays.
The essays grade Ms. Okafor.
Ms. Okafor is graded by the essays.
Grades the essays, Ms. Okafor.
Ms. Okafor performs the action in present tense, so she is the subject.
Which sentence is the active-voice version? The canoe was paddled across the lake by my uncle.
My uncle paddled the canoe across the lake.
The canoe paddled my uncle across the lake.
My uncle was paddled across the lake by the canoe.
Across the lake paddled the canoe my uncle.
My uncle is the doer, so he becomes the subject of the active sentence.
Which sentence is the active-voice version? The question was answered by Priya.
Priya answered the question.
The question answered Priya.
Priya was answered by the question.
Answered the question Priya did.
Priya performs the action, so she moves to the subject position.
Which sentence is the active-voice version? The lights will be turned off by the last person.
The last person will turn off the lights.
The lights will turn off the last person.
The last person will be turned off by the lights.
Will turn off the lights the last person.
The last person is the doer, and the future tense is kept.
Which sentence is the active-voice version? The movie was enjoyed by the whole family.
The whole family enjoyed the movie.
The movie enjoyed the whole family.
The whole family was enjoyed by the movie.
Enjoyed the movie the whole family.
The family does the enjoying, so the family becomes the subject.
Which sentence is the active-voice version? The school was closed by the blizzard.
The blizzard closed the school.
The school closed the blizzard.
The blizzard was closed by the school.
Closed the school, the blizzard.
The blizzard caused the action, so it becomes the subject.
Which sentence is the active-voice version? Our tent was knocked over by a moose.
A moose knocked over our tent.
Our tent knocked over a moose.
A moose was knocked over by our tent.
Knocked over our tent a moose.
The moose performs the action, so it becomes the subject.
Which sentence is the active-voice version? The invitations have been mailed by Aunt Rosa.
Aunt Rosa has mailed the invitations.
The invitations have mailed Aunt Rosa.
Aunt Rosa has been mailed by the invitations.
Mailed the invitations Aunt Rosa has.
Aunt Rosa becomes the subject, and the present perfect has mailed is kept.
Which sentence is the active-voice version? The goal was scored by the youngest player.
The youngest player scored the goal.
The goal scored the youngest player.
The youngest player was scored by the goal.
Scored the goal the youngest player.
The player does the scoring, so the player becomes the subject.
Which sentence is the active-voice version? The problem is being solved by the engineers.
The engineers are solving the problem.
The problem is solving the engineers.
The engineers are being solved by the problem.
Solving the problem are the engineers.
The engineers are the doers, and the progressive tense becomes are solving.
Which sentence is the active-voice version? The house was cleaned by the twins.
The twins cleaned the house.
The house cleaned the twins.
The twins were cleaned by the house.
Cleaned the house the twins.
The twins perform the action, so they become the subject.
Which sentence is the active-voice version? The flag is raised by a student every morning.
A student raises the flag every morning.
The flag raises a student every morning.
A student is raised by the flag every morning.
Raises the flag a student every morning.
A student does the raising, so the student becomes the subject in present tense.
engPRL: Which sentence uses parallel structure?
On weekends, Omar likes to sleep in, to read comics, and to play hockey.
On weekends, Omar likes to sleep in, reading comics, and to play hockey.
On weekends, Omar likes sleeping in, to read comics, and playing hockey.
On weekends, Omar likes to sleep in, read comics, and playing hockey.

Which sentence uses parallel structure?
The trail was steep, rocky, and muddy.
The trail was steep, rocky, and full of mud.
The trail was steep, had rocks, and muddy.
The trail was steep, rocky, and it had mud.
All three items are single adjectives.
Which sentence uses parallel structure?
She wants to travel, to learn, and to grow.
She wants to travel, learning, and to grow.
She wants travelling, to learn, and growing.
She wants to travel, to learn, and growth.
Each item is an infinitive, so the list is parallel.
Which sentence uses parallel structure?
We cleaned the kitchen, swept the floor, and folded the laundry.
We cleaned the kitchen, sweeping the floor, and folded the laundry.
We cleaned the kitchen, swept the floor, and the laundry was folded.
We cleaned the kitchen, the floor was swept, and folding the laundry.

Which sentence uses parallel structure?
Not only is the book funny, but it is also wise.
Not only is the book funny, but also it has wisdom.
Not only funny, but the book is also wise.
The book not only is funny, but also wisdom.
